chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq said:

I asked him and said: We send dirhams to Ahwaz, which has an exchange rate, and goods are purchased for us with them. Then we write a ledger (ruznamaja) on which the exchange rate of the dirhams is noted. When we sell, we must mention the exchange rate of the dirhams in the markup sale (murabahah), and it will suffice for us regarding that. He said: 'If it is a markup sale (murabahah), inform him of that; and if it is a bargaining sale (musawamah), there is no harm.'

key_terms.الْمُرَابَحَةِ: Markup sale (selling at a known profit margin)
key_terms.الْمُسَاوَمَةً: Bargaining sale (selling at a negotiated price without specifying cost)

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to disclose the original cost and exchange rate when selling goods at a fixed markup in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the transparency requirements in commercial transactions, specifically distinguishing between *murabahah* (cost-plus sale) and *musawamah* (bargaining). The Imam instructs that when selling via markup, the seller must disclose the initial cost and the applied exchange rate (particularly relevant for currency conversion to Ahwaz), whereas in general bargaining, such disclosure is not obligatory. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on honesty and preventing deception in trade, ensuring the buyer understands the basis of the price in fixed-margin sales.
